_comment: Web-sourced (secondary) inputs for tools/macro_policy.py. Primary hosts (federalreserve.gov, bls.gov, bea.gov) are blocked by policy; every fact here is from WebSearch result summaries and is SECONDARY-SOURCED. Release dates in 'catalysts' come from the FRED release calendar (fred.stlouisfed.org, times shown there in US Central; converted to ET here).  Updated 2026-11-05: new run 2026-11-04 (no new scored macro release since the 2026-10-28 run); catalyst dates re-checked against FRED release calendars on 2026-11-05.

fed.action_basis: Hold at 3.75-4.00 after the 2026-09-16 hike; two voters preferred a 25bp hike; statement: inflation 'remains elevated', activity upgraded to 'expanding at a strong pace', Committee awaiting 'accumulation of more information'.
fed.dissenters: Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack, each preferring a 25bp hike
fed.guidance_basis: Spec guidance_classification.hawkish: 'at least two voters prefer a hike' is met (2). Statement is data-dependent ('accumulation of more information'), not explicit likely tightening, so 75 not 90. October minutes not yet released, so no minutes adjustment.
fed.guidance_statement_basis: Statement-only reading from guidance_basis: data-dependent ('accumulation of more information'), no stated tightening bias; the hawkish classification comes from the spec's 'at least two voters prefer a hike' rule, applied in code.

2026-11-03._comment: Run as-of 2026-11-04 close. fed_communications_since_decision._note: Context only, NOT scored: the spec's guidance subscore uses the statement, press conference and minutes. Speeches by non-dissenting officials do not change guidance, votes or dissent counts. Secondary-sourced.

market_context_narrative_only._note: For the Supervisor's narrative only. NOT a scored input to any module (spec: do not raise MacroRisk because SPY or QQQ fell). Secondary news; intraday figures differ by capture time.

events.summary: Tech-led selloff: S&P 500 -1.8% to 7,580.07, Nasdaq Composite about -2.9%. Drivers cited: rare earnings misses at Amazon and Alphabet plus Intel and ServiceNow disappointments, renewed doubt about Big Tech AI spending, rotation into defensives and energy. Same day Logan and Musalem called for more hikes.
events.corroboration: S&P 500 close 7,580.07 matches FRED SP500 and the Robinhood SPX bar for 2026-10-30

events.summary: US midterm Election Day; S&P 500 snapped a 3-day losing streak as chip stocks rebounded (close 7,568.92).

Post-election rally: S&P 500 +1.6% to 7,688.62 (Robinhood SPX bar, not interpolated). Several reports describe the midterm outcome as a Democratic sweep; the election outcome itself was not confirmed by an election-results source in this search.

Intraday (session open) chip/AI rout: Nasdaq Composite about -3.6% to -4.2% by late morning ET, trading more than 10% below its October record (correction territory; second correction of 2026 if confirmed at the close); S&P 500 about -2% to -2.9%; Dow down more than 1,000 points at one point. Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down more than 11% at one point; Qualcomm -9% to -11% on a weak outlook; AMD about -12% despite record results; Nvidia about -6% to -7%; CoreWeave lower. Drivers cited: AI capex and return worries, heightened scrutiny of data-center expansion and possible AI regulation after the midterms, higher borrowing costs. Figures are intraday, not closes.
